title: Nikkei falls 1% as SoftBank sinks 6%: is Japan’s AI trade starting to crack?
source_used: Reuters (text read on the Metrobank Wealth Insights news page)
key_facts: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.06% to 68,308.92 in early trading on Friday 9 Oct 2026, on course for a slight weekly decline.
SoftBank Group, a major investor in OpenAI, was the largest loser on the index, sinking 5.40%.
US stocks fell overnight, dragged by technology companies after a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue was $20 billion less than previously signalled.
Sony Financial Group analysts said reports that a major unlisted AI company's revenue fell short of its own forecasts set off a chain reaction of selling in related stocks.
Stress in global bond markets, higher oil prices and concern about France's budget also weighed on sentiment.
Japan's August household spending fell 3.1% year on year.
quote_evidence: Reports that a major unlisted AI company's revenue fell short of its own forecasts triggered a chain reaction of selling in related stocks
The largest loser on the Nikkei was SoftBank Group, a major investor in OpenAI, which sank 5.40% and dragged on the index.
why_it_matters_hint: The OpenAI revenue story spread from Wall Street to Tokyo through shares of SoftBank, a big OpenAI investor.
notes: Invezz page blocked by Cloudflare; Reuters report on the same trading day read on the Metrobank site (Reuters original link not available). Invezz reported SoftBank down about 6% and the Nikkei down 1%; Reuters early-trade figures used here.
